messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: Priya Shah <priya.shah@mayatech.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: November OKR pulse: product & eng roadmap status, launch contingencies

Team —

Quick pulse ahead of the QBR pack deadline (next Tue). Attached is a compact snapshot of the current product & eng deliverables tied to this quarter's OKRs and the live contingency tracker. Key points: 

- OKR progress: Feature set A (search reranking) is ~85% complete against scope; embeddings infra work has a 2-week drift against plan.
- Delivery risks: we have a throughput regression in the 2nd-stage KV caching rollout (infra) that can impact peak-latency SLAs for Dedicated customers.
- Customer impact: Mayatech integration depends on the cached responses; they asked for a firm timeline by EOD Thursday.

Asks (short):
- Karthik: brief mitigation plan and ETA for the KV caching rollback vs fix by 10:30 today.
- Monica: confirm customer communication approach for Mayatech and any immediate credits/wrapping ask.
- Vivek/Laura: flag anything we need to call out in the QBR slides (risk, exec decision points).

I've attached the full snapshot and the contingency tracker — please edit the contingency sheet directly (I added a short legend). We'll run a 30m alignment at 3pm PT today if you can make it; otherwise drop updates in-thread.

Attachments: [Attachment: 2027-11-02_product-roadmap-snapshot.pdf (application/pdf)], [Attachment: deployment_contingency_tracker.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]

Thanks,
Ben
Ben Carter
Head of Product Strategy
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com
Cc: vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 02 Nov 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: November OKR pulse: product & eng roadmap status, launch contingencies

Ben —

Thanks for the snapshot. Short update on the KV caching regression: during the staged rollout we observed a 12–18% token throughput drop when the long-tail cache miss path exercised a new eviction policy on certain model sizes. Immediate mitigations in flight:

- Roll back the eviction policy change for Dedicated pools (targeted rollback window: tonight, 10pm PT).
- Backfill monitoring alert that captures sequence-length skew causing the miss-rate spike (complete by 3pm).
- If rollback insufficient, we have a patch to the cache prefetch heuristic ready; testing now, ETA for rollout 48 hours.

Impact: if rollback executes cleanly, user-facing latency should return to baseline and the Mayatech integration timeline is preserved; if rollback is blocked (capacity limits tonight), we should expect a 3–5 day slip on the integration ETA. I will post a short runbook note in the contingency tracker and link the JIRA.

Karthik
Staff Engineer, Serving Runtime

A 48-hour contingency is workable but anything beyond that forces us to reschedule a key exec demo (which would be costly for our timeline).

Thanks, everyone — consolidation and next steps: 

1) Karthik: proceed with the targeted rollback tonight and confirm completion in-thread. If rollback fails, escalate to infra ops and trigger the patch; ETA for patch = 48h. Link: JIRA INF-5427.
2) Monica: publish the Mayatech-facing note and share the sandbox token by EOD Thurs if rollback shows any risk.
3) Vivek/Laura: I'll highlight the regression and the fallback approach in the QBR slides under "Delivery Risks"; flag if you want a sharper ask (e.g., approval for partial credits for impacted customers).
4) Priya: 3pm PT today works — please have your integration lead join; call invite sent. If we need to shift, we'll communicate before 11am PT.

I'll update the contingency tracker as items resolve and post a short exec note once we verify rollback health. Thanks for rapid responses — this is the sort of cross-team coordination we need for a clean QBR narrative.

Ben
Head of Product Strategy
Redwood Inference
